DEFAULT_ENV_NAMES gains OMP_PROFILE and nothing else (config.mjs:10-13), with the reason beside it (:3-9). The plugin spawns the child with pickEnv(config.env) (index.mjs:73), and pickEnv copies only listed names that exist in the plugin's own environment (gateway-client.mjs:26-33), so OMP_PROFILE reaches the child only when the launcher set it; under hcom-seat's dsh role that value is the lever's own OMP_PROFILE=dsh, set under env -i (hcom-seat:2895, which since U318 also carries CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, the shared directory). The list still names no credential: the use-case test asserts no KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, OAUTH or PASSWORD name (test/use-cases.test.mjs:622-626), and the new recorder test asserts the child carries OMP_PROFILE when the plugin has it and not when it is unset, with a non-row name dropped (test/gateway-client.test.mjs:251-283). The value moves the child from ~/.omp/agent, which the dsh role denies, to ~/.omp/profiles/dsh, which the role already grants for read and write (hcom-seat:2050, :2396) and which the judge pins to its own position (:2412-2418); srt still denies every other profile, so a different value would fail as the g6 run did, not widen. The row's `env` can replace the list (config.mjs:37), but the profile file is the operator's managed file, and a value only ever comes from the plugin's own environment. Outside hcom-seat, an operator running dsh directly forwards their own OMP_PROFILE to their own child.

hardening_notes: With OMP_PROFILE=dsh the gateway child keeps its omp state, agent.db and whatever login state omp stores there, in ~/.omp/profiles/dsh, a dsh write root the contained session can read and rewrite (hcom-seat:2050, :2396). The child's environment carries no token name, so its Claude login is read from that profile or from a source this run may not inspect. If it is a stored refresh credential, it is a second copy of the operator's login inside the sandbox (since U312 and U318 the shim exports no token; the seats' login is the shared directory's, the U318 candidate of this run), and it would outlive the launch. Both downloads derive from one URL (aws_cli_url :61; the .sig is the URL plus .sig, :154-157), a write-once versioned object, so the round-1 hazard of pairing one release's archive with another's signature (the unversioned latest objects are rewritten minutes apart) is gone. The key file's fingerprint must equal the pinned AWS_CLI_FINGERPRINT (:20, rendered from assets.aws-cli in agent-config.yaml:1213-1217), be valid and unexpired (:160-169), before gpgv verifies the signature over the archive (:170-171), every step with its status returned.
